욥기-22-1.title: 욥기 22장 1절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-1.exegesis: 34. falsehood-- literally, "transgression." Your boasted "consolations" ( Job 15:11 ) are contradicted by facts ("vain"); they therefore only betray your evil intent ("wickedness") against me.
욥기-22-1.theologicalNote: 34. falsehood-- literally, "transgression." Your boasted "consolations" ( Job 15:11 ) are contradicted by facts ("vain"); they therefore only betray your evil intent ("wickedness") against me.

욥기-22-2.title: 욥기 22장 2절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 22 THIRD SERIES. Job 22:1-30 . As Before, Eliphaz Begins. 1. Eliphaz shows that man's goodness does not add to, or man's badness take from, the happiness of God; therefore it cannot be that God sends prosperity to some and calamities on others for His own advantage; the cause of the goods and ills sent must lie in the men themselves ( Psa 16:2 ; Lu 17:10 ; Ac 17:25 ; 1Ch 29:14 ). So Job's calamities must arise from guilt. Eliphaz, instead of meeting the facts, tries to show that it could not be so.

욥기-22-3.title: 욥기 22장 3절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-3.exegesis: 2. as he that is wise-- rather, yea the pious man profiteth himself. So "understanding" or "wise"--pious ( Da 12:3 , 10 ; Psa 14:2 ) [Michaelis].
욥기-22-3.theologicalNote: 2. as he that is wise-- rather, yea the pious man profiteth himself. So "understanding" or "wise"--pious ( Da 12:3 , 10 ; Psa 14:2 ) [Michaelis].

욥기-22-4.title: 욥기 22장 4절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-4.exegesis: 3. pleasure-- accession of happiness; God has pleasure in man's righteousness ( Psa 45:7 ), but He is not dependent on man's character for His happiness.
욥기-22-4.theologicalNote: 3. pleasure-- accession of happiness; God has pleasure in man's righteousness ( Psa 45:7 ), but He is not dependent on man's character for His happiness.

욥기-22-5.title: 욥기 22장 5절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-5.exegesis: 4. Is the punishment inflicted on thee from fear of thee, in order to disarm thee? as Job had implied (see on Job 7:12 ; Job 7:20 ; and Job 10:17 ). will he enter ... into judgment?-- Job had desired this ( Job 13:3 , 21 ). He ought rather to have spoken as in Psa 143:2 .

욥기-22-6.title: 욥기 22장 6절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-6.exegesis: 5. Heretofore Eliphaz had only insinuated, now he plainly asserts Job's guilt, merely on the ground of his sufferings.
욥기-22-6.theologicalNote: 5. Heretofore Eliphaz had only insinuated, now he plainly asserts Job's guilt, merely on the ground of his sufferings.

욥기-22-7.title: 욥기 22장 7절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-7.exegesis: 6. The crimes alleged, on a harsh inference, by Eliphaz against Job are such as he would think likely to be committed by a rich man. The Mosaic law ( Ex 22:26 ; De 24:10 ) subsequently embodied the feeling that existed among the godly in Job's time against oppression of debtors as to their pledges. Here the case is not quite the same; Job is charged with taking a pledge where he had no just claim to it; and in the second clause, that pledge (the outer garment which served the poor as a covering by day and a bed by night) is represented as taken from one who had not "changes of raiment" (a common constituent of wealth in the East), but was poorly clad-- "naked" ( Mt 25:36 ; Jas 2:15 ); a sin the more heinous in a rich man like Job.

욥기-22-8.title: 욥기 22장 8절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-8.exegesis: 7. Hospitality to the weary traveller is regarded in the East as a primary duty ( Is 21:14 ).
욥기-22-8.theologicalNote: 7. Hospitality to the weary traveller is regarded in the East as a primary duty ( Is 21:14 ).

욥기-22-9.title: 욥기 22장 9절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-9.exegesis: 8. mighty-- Hebrew, "man of arm" ( Psa 10:15 ; namely, Job). honourable-- Hebrew, "eminent, or, accepted for countenance" ( Is 3:3 ; 2Ki 5:1 ); that is, possessing authority. Eliphaz repeats his charge ( Job 15:28 ; so Zophar, Job 20:19 ), that it was by violence Job wrung houses and lands from the poor, to whom now he refused relief ( Job 22:7 , 9 ) [Michaelis].

욥기-22-10.title: 욥기 22장 10절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-10.exegesis: 9. empty-- without their wants being relieved ( Ge 31:42 ). The Mosaic law especially protected the widow and fatherless ( Ex 22:22 ); the violation of it in their case by the great is a complaint of the prophets ( Is 1:17 ). arms-- supports, helps, on which one leans ( Ho 7:15 ). Thou hast robbed them of their only stay. Job replies in Job 29:11-16 .

욥기-22-11.title: 욥기 22장 11절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-11.exegesis: 10. snares-- alluding to Job's admission ( Job 19:6 ; compare Job 18:10 ; Pr 22:5 ).
욥기-22-11.theologicalNote: 10. snares-- alluding to Job's admission ( Job 19:6 ; compare Job 18:10 ; Pr 22:5 ).

욥기-22-12.title: 욥기 22장 12절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-12.exegesis: 11. that-- so that thou. abundance-- floods. Danger by floods is a less frequent image in this book than in the rest of the Old Testament ( Job 11:16 ; 27:20 ).
욥기-22-12.theologicalNote: 11. that-- so that thou. abundance-- floods. Danger by floods is a less frequent image in this book than in the rest of the Old Testament ( Job 11:16 ; 27:20 ).

욥기-22-13.title: 욥기 22장 13절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-13.exegesis: 12. Eliphaz says this to prove that God can from His height behold all things; gratuitously inferring that Job denied it, because he denied that the wicked are punished here. height-- Hebrew, "head of the stars"; that is, "elevation" ( Job 11:8 ).

욥기-22-14.title: 욥기 22장 14절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-14.exegesis: 13. Rather, And yet thou sayest, God does not concern Himself with ("know") human affairs ( Psa 73:11 ).
욥기-22-14.theologicalNote: 13. Rather, And yet thou sayest, God does not concern Himself with ("know") human affairs ( Psa 73:11 ).

욥기-22-15.title: 욥기 22장 15절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-15.exegesis: 14. in the circuit of heaven-- only, not taking any part in earthly affairs. Job is alleged as holding this Epicurean sentiment ( La 3:44 ; Is 29:15 ; 40:27 ; Jr 23:24 ; Eze 8:12 ; Psa 139:12 ).
욥기-22-15.theologicalNote: 14. in the circuit of heaven-- only, not taking any part in earthly affairs. Job is alleged as holding this Epicurean sentiment ( La 3:44 ; Is 29:15 ; 40:27 ; Jr 23:24 ; Eze 8:12 ; Psa 139:12 ).

욥기-22-16.title: 욥기 22장 16절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-16.exegesis: 15. marked-- Rather, Dost thou keep to? that is, wish to follow (so Hebrew, 2Sa 22:22 ). If so, beware of sharing their end. the old way-- the degenerate ways of the world before the flood ( Ge 6:5 ).

욥기-22-17.title: 욥기 22장 17절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-17.exegesis: 16. cut down-- rather, "fettered," as in Job 16:8 ; that is, arrested by death. out of time-- prematurely, suddenly ( Job 15:32 ; Ec 7:17 ); literally, "whose foundation was poured out (so as to become) a stream or flood." The solid earth passed from beneath their feet into a flood ( Ge 7:11 ).

욥기-22-18.title: 욥기 22장 18절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-18.exegesis: 17. Eliphaz designedly uses Job's own words ( Job 21:14 , 15 ). do for them-- They think they can do everything for themselves.
욥기-22-18.theologicalNote: 17. Eliphaz designedly uses Job's own words ( Job 21:14 , 15 ). do for them-- They think they can do everything for themselves.

욥기-22-19.title: 욥기 22장 19절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-19.exegesis: 18. "Yet" you say (see on Job 21:16 ) that it is "He who filled their houses with good"-- "their good is not in their hand," but comes from God. but the counsel ... is-- rather, "may the counsel be," &c. Eliphaz sarcastically quotes in continuation Job's words ( Job 21:16 ). Yet, after uttering this godless sentiment, thou dost hypocritically add, "May the counsel," &c.

욥기-22-20.title: 욥기 22장 20절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-20.exegesis: 19. Triumph of the pious at the fall of the recent followers of the antediluvian sinners. While in the act of denying that God can do them any good or harm, they are cut off by Him. Eliphaz hereby justifies himself and the friends for their conduct to Job: not derision of the wretched, but joy at the vindication of God's ways ( Psa 107:42 ; Re 15:3 ; 16:7 ; 19:1 , 2).

욥기-22-21.title: 욥기 22장 21절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-21.exegesis: 20. The triumphant speech of the pious. If "substance" be retained, translate, rather as the Septuagint, "Has not their substance been taken away, and ... ?" But the Hebrew is rather, "Truly our adversary is cut down" [Gesenius]. The same opposition exists between the godly and ungodly seed as between the unfallen and restored Adam and Satan (adversary); this forms the groundwork of the book ( Job 1:1-2:13 ; Ge 3:15 ). remnant-- all that "is left" of the sinner; repeated from Job 20:26 , which makes Umbreit's rendering "glory" (Margin), "excellency," less probable. fire-- alluding to Job ( Job 1:16 ; 15:34 ; 18:15). First is mentioned destruction by water ( Job 22:16 ); here, by fire ( 2Pe 3:5-7 ).

욥기-22-22.title: 욥기 22장 22절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-22.exegesis: 21. Eliphaz takes it for granted, Job is not yet "acquainted" with God; literally, "become a companion of God." Turn with familiar confidence to God. and be-- So thou shalt be: the second imperatively expresses the consequence of obeying the first ( Psa 37:27 ). peace-- prosperity and restoration to Job; true spiritually also to us ( Ro 5:1 ; Col 1:20 ). good-- ( 1Ti 4:8 ).

욥기-22-24.title: 욥기 22장 24절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-24.exegesis: 23. Built up-- anew, as a restored house. thou shalt put away-- rather, "If thou put away" [Michaelis].
욥기-22-24.theologicalNote: 23. Built up-- anew, as a restored house. thou shalt put away-- rather, "If thou put away" [Michaelis].

욥기-22-25.title: 욥기 22장 25절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-25.exegesis: 24. Rather, containing the protasis from the last clause of Job 22:23 , "If thou regard the glittering metal as dust"; literally, "lay it on on the dust"; to regard it of as little value as the dust on which it lies. The apodosis is at Job 22:25 , Then shall the Almighty be, &c. God will take the place of the wealth, in which thou didst formerly trust. gold-- rather, "precious" or "glittering metal," parallel to "(gold) of Ophir," in the second clause [Umbreit and Maurer]. Ophir-- derived from a Hebrew word "dust," namely, gold dust. Heeren thinks it a general name for the rich countries of the South, on the African, Indian, and especially the Arabian coast (where was the port Aphar. El Ophir, too, a city of Oman, was formerly the center of Arabian commerce). It is curious that the natives of Malacca still call their mines Ophirs. stones of the brooks-- If thou dost let the gold of Ophir remain in its native valley among the stones of the brooks; that is, regard it as of little worth as the stones, &c. The gold was washed down by mountain torrents and lodged among the stones and sand of the valley.

욥기-22-26.title: 욥기 22장 26절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-26.exegesis: 25. Apodosis. Yea-- rather, Then shall the Almighty be, &c. defence-- rather, as the same Hebrew means in Job 22:24 (see on Job 22:24 )--Thy precious metals; God will be to thee in the place of riches. plenty of silver-- rather, "And shall be to thee in the place of laboriously-obtained treasures of silver" [Gesenius]. Elegantly implying, it is less labor to find God than the hidden metals; at least to the humble seeker ( Job 28:12-28 ). But [Maurer] "the shining silver."

욥기-22-27.title: 욥기 22장 27절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-27.exegesis: 26. lift up ... face, &c.-- repeated from Zophar ( Job 11:15 ).
욥기-22-27.theologicalNote: 26. lift up ... face, &c.-- repeated from Zophar ( Job 11:15 ).

욥기-22-28.title: 욥기 22장 28절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-28.exegesis: 27. ( Is 58:9 , 14 ). pay thy vows-- which thou hast promised to God in the event of thy prayers being heard: God will give thee occasion to pay the former, by hearing the latter.
욥기-22-28.theologicalNote: 27. ( Is 58:9 , 14 ). pay thy vows-- which thou hast promised to God in the event of thy prayers being heard: God will give thee occasion to pay the former, by hearing the latter.

욥기-22-30.title: 욥기 22장 30절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-22-30.exegesis: 29. Rather, When (thy ways; from Job 22:28 ) are cast down (for a time), thou shalt (soon again have joyful cause to) say, There is lifting up (prosperity returns back to me) [Maurer]. he-- God. humble-- Hebrew, "him that is of low eyes." Eliphaz implies that Job is not so now in his affliction; therefore it continues: with this he contrasts the blessed effect of being humble under it ( Jas 4:6 ; 1Pe 5:5 probably quote this passage). Therefore it is better, I think, to take the first clause as referred to by "God resisteth the proud." When (men) are cast down, thou shalt say (behold the effects of) pride. Eliphaz hereby justifies himself for attributing Job's calamities to his pride. "Giveth grace to the humble," answers to the second clause.
